definitions.gloss: economic effect; economic impact; economic benefit
definitions.explanation: The measurable influence that an event, policy, or project has on the economy, typically expressed in monetary terms.

examples.japanese: オリンピックの{経済効果|けいざいこうか}は{大|おお}きい。
examples.english: The economic impact of the Olympics is enormous.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{駅|えき}の{開業|かいぎょう}による{経済効果|けいざいこうか}は{数十億円|すうじゅうおくえん}と{試算|しさん}された。
examples.english: The economic effect of the new station opening was estimated at tens of billions of yen.

examples.japanese: {観光|かんこう}による{経済効果|けいざいこうか}を{高|たか}めるために、{地域|ちいき}を{挙|あ}げてイベントを{企画|きかく}した。
examples.english: To boost the economic impact of tourism, the entire region planned events together.

notes:
A compound of {経済|けいざい} (economy) + {効果|こうか} (effect). Very common in news and policy discussions, often used to quantify the financial benefit of major events, infrastructure projects, or government policies. Japanese media frequently report {経済効果|けいざいこうか} figures for things like the World Cup, cherry blossom season, or new bullet train routes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {経済効果|けいざいこうか}が{大|おお}きい: the economic effect is significant
- {経済効果|けいざいこうか}を{見込|みこ}む: to expect economic benefits
- {経済効果|けいざいこうか}を{試算|しさん}する: to estimate the economic impact
- {経済効果|けいざいこうか}を{高|たか}める: to boost the economic effect
- {波及|はきゅう}{経済効果|けいざいこうか}: ripple economic effect

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {経済的影響|けいざいてきえいきょう}: economic influence (more neutral; can be negative or positive)
- {景気効果|けいきこうか}: business stimulus effect (focuses on stimulating the economy)
- {費用対効果|ひようたいこうか}: cost-effectiveness (ratio of cost to benefit)
